Why Cave Creek is its own job

Cave Creek is a dust town, and pretending otherwise is how cleaners get fired.

Half of Cave Creek sits on graded desert with unpaved shoulders, washes that move after every monsoon, and a lot of homes with big south-facing glass. Fine grit gets in through door sweeps and window tracks whatever anyone does, and it settles on the horizontal edges nobody looks at — fan blades, door tops, the ledge above a shower surround. That is precisely the list a deep clean covers and a two-hour tidy does not, which is why almost every Cave Creek house we take on starts with one.

It is also why we recommend a deep clean here every three months rather than four. It is not upselling; it is the wash schedule.
